scope: Narrow independent audit of PAdES CRL interval applicability at current UTC (§12.8.3.4.7) versus later-issued CRL use for historical signer validation (§12.8.3.4.8). No global RFC 5280 freshness change is proposed.

current_clause.rule: For current-UTC validation, a CRL is appropriate only when current UTC is in the interval delimited by thisUpdate and nextUpdate.

historical_clause.rule: For a past validation instant, CRL applicability requires capture before signer-certificate expiry and nextUpdate after the historical instant. It does not say thisUpdate must be before that past instant.

source.ec3_annotations: The EC3 annotation inventory has only cross-reference links on physical pages 598–599; no erratum modifies either CRL time condition.

cases.name: current_utc_must_be_inside_both_crl_bounds
cases.evidence: crates/pdf-signature/src/revocation/tests.rs::fixtures::{CA,GOOD_LEAF,CRL}; the CRL is signed by the fixture CA, thisUpdate is 2026-06-01, nextUpdate 2036-06-01, and the CA/leaf are valid from 2026-01-01 through 2036-01-01.
cases.control: The existing current-in-window control asks at 2026-10-01 and expects Good. This remains required.
cases.discriminating_input: Ask as current UTC at 2026-03-01: the chain certificates are current, but CRL.thisUpdate is in the future. EC3 .7 says this CRL is not appropriate for this current-time check.
cases.implementation: revocation::from_list checks only whether at is later than nextUpdate. It does not reject at < thisUpdate, so it returns Good for the March current-time case.
cases.verdict: Context-specific conformance gap candidate. Current PAdES callers need a current-UTC applicability check; a single undifferentiated instant is insufficient to encode both .7 and .8.

cases.name: historical_validation_may_use_later_issued_crl
cases.evidence: Same genuinely signed CRL and same fixture CA/leaf. At 2026-03-01, the leaf is already within its validity period and the CRL nextUpdate is after the historical instant. The low-level fixture does not encode a PDF DSS capture time, so this is an applicability control only, not a complete §.8 capture-before-expiry test.
cases.control: Existing revocation/tests.rs::a_list_issued_after_the_instant_asked_about_is_evidence_about_it is a historical-time control, but it currently uses 2025, before its test certificates' 2026 notBefore. The March 2026 value is a stronger valid-certificate-time low-level control: it is after notBefore and before thisUpdate. The test does not build the complete certificate path or encode the DSS capture time.
cases.rule: §12.8.3.4.8 only requires pre-expiry capture and nextUpdate after the historical instant. Preserve acceptance of this later-issued CRL for the historical signer-time case.
cases.verdict: Do not add a global at >= thisUpdate rule to from_list; it would break the historical case.

caller_trace: viewer-core/src/notes.rs::signatures initializes BestSignatureTime::now(host_now); if an established signature or document timestamp provides an earlier time, it selects that past instant instead.

viewer-core/src/notes.rs::about_one calls Signature::trust with asked.when.at(); signature.rs passes that instant to trust::validate_constrained; trust::Search::walk calls revocation::status_within for every path certificate.

viewer-core/src/notes.rs::signature_timestamps_instant validates the timestamp authority path using AskedAt::TheCallersInstant(now), so the timestamp-authority path is a current-time check even when its genTime later supplies a past signer-validation instant.

revocation::status/status_within expose only an Instant plus policy Issuance. They do not represent whether that instant means current UTC or an authenticated historical time. Other policy callers (e.g. Issuance::fresh_after for REQ-4.2-03) have separate issuance constraints; they are not a reason to apply .7's current-UTC lower bound globally.
